div.head: Grið 4
div.ab: ⁊ þus hit stod on ðam dagum inne mid Englum, ðæt, gyf feorhscyldig man cyning gesohte, arcebiscop oððon æþeling, þonne ahte he nigon nihta grið feore to gebeorge, butan him se cyng rumran fyrstes geunnan wolde.

And þus hit stod on ðam dagum inne mid Englum ðæt gyf feorhscyldig man cyning gesohte, arcebiscop, oððon æþeling, þonne ahte he nigon nihta grið feore to gebeorge, butan him se cyng rumran fyrstes geunnan wolde.

Und es galt in jenen Tagen im Lande bei den Engländern folgendermassen, dass, wenn ein Mensch, [der] das Leben verwirkt [hatte], den König, einen Erzbischof oder Prinzen [um Schutz] aufsuchte, dann hatte er 9 Nächte Sonderfrieden, dem Leben zum Schutze, ausser wenn ihm der König weitere Frist gewähren wollte.

And in those days in the land among the English it held as follows: that if a person [who had] forfeited his life sought out the king, an archbishop or a prince [for protection], then he had 9 nights' special peace to protect his life, unless the king wished to grant him a longer respite.

And it so stood in those days among the English that if a condemned man sought the king, the archbishop, or a nobleman, then he had nine nights’ sanctuary in which to save his life, unless the king wished to grant him more time.
